name: Japanese crowdsourcing localization and ranking manipulation

attribution.legal_posture: This record summarizes Koike’s NEC research into Japanese-language crowdsourcing activity attributed to DPRK IT workers

ttps: Acquire or repurpose established accounts belonging to real people
Build long-lived platform reputation and obtain top-tier or PRO worker badges
Discover linked accounts through public ranking/thank-you logs
Mutually press “thank you” or ranking buttons across linked worker accounts
Rely on machine translation for Japanese-language profiles and client interactions
Reuse profile templates containing unnatural Japanese phrasing
Translate Korean through English into Japanese, leaving word-order and vocabulary artifacts
Use AI-generated, anime, free-stock, or composited profile images
Use local business social networks to advertise claimed startup achievements
Use local-language services because Japanese employers search in Japanese
caveats: Each signal can occur benignly; use the set as a composite detection aid rather than a nationality proxy.

infrastructure.value: Japanese-language marketplaces with anonymous registration and public worker rankings
